newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghanistan's Taleban says attack repulsed.
newsitem.headline: Afghanistan's Taleban says attack repulsed.

text.p: A commander of the Islamic Taleban militia said on Saturday that its fighters had repulsed a three-pronged attack launched by the opposition alliance.
Taleban Commander Mohammed Usman told Reuters the opposition forces launched their attack early on Friday.
"The combined forces of the opposition launched a major offensive at 3.45 (2315 GMT Thursday) yesterday morning," Usman said.

"At the beginning of the attack the enemy gained some ground, but once the Taleban received reinforcements, they were pushed back and the front line is now in the same place as before the attack." he said.
It was not possible to independently verify Usman's comments.

The Taleban have been fighting forces loyal to the ousted government of President Burhauddin Rabbani and their new ally General Abdul Rashid Dostum since the Taleban took Kabul six weeks ago and moved further north.

Attempts by the United Nations to broker a ceasefire between the two sides have so far had little effect although there has been a face-to-face meeting between the belligerents in the Pakistani capital Islamabad.

Usman said the opposition had tried to take the villages of Qaloqan and Istalif, 25 km (18 miles) north of Kabul, and were hoping to cut the main supply route to the eastern side of the Taleban front line, the so-called "new road".
The Taleban are facing the opposition along a front line that follows a low range of hills that bisect the broad valley running north of Kabul to the foothills of the Hindu Kush.
This week, the Taleban managed to take five km (three miles) of territory from the opposition, including Qaloqan and Istalif.
Usman said the fighting for the new road and Qaloqan ended after five hours, but the battle for Istalif lasted all day.
Istalif, once a resort for Kabulis and famed for its delicate blue pottery, lies on the slopes of the mountains to the west of the valley. It commands a broad view over the whole battlefront.
Opposition forces were using artillery and rocket launchers based in Istalif to bombard Taleban positions.
The front lines were quiet on Saturday morning. Artillery commander Usman was using the break in hostilities to sit in the sun in the lee of the small, mud-walled hut that serves as his command post.
